title: Eid al-Fitr: the day
hookLine: ghusl, perfume, best clothes, eating before prayer, a different road back (Bukhari)

cards: A small detail, tucked into Sahih al-Bukhari, in a report from Jabir. On the day of Eid, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, went out to the prayer by one road and came home by another. That's the whole report.
No reason given. Just two roads. Before that walk, there's a morning to get through: water, clothes, something sweet to eat.
Today, the morning of Eid al-Fitr, the feast that breaks the fast, one small act at a time.

teach.h: WATER: A GHUSL BEFORE GOING OUT.
teach.b: Start with water. In the Muwatta of Imam Malik, Ibn 'Umar, a companion of the Prophet, would take a full bath, a ghusl, on the morning of the Fitr before going out to the prayer. The day begins clean.

teach.h: CLOTHES: A DAY YOU DRESS FOR.
teach.b: Then clothes. In al-Bukhari, 'Umar finds a fine cloak in the market and brings it to the Prophet, saying, in paraphrase: buy this, and dress up in it for Eid and for receiving visitors.
The Prophet turned that one down, because it was silk. But notice what 'Umar took for granted: Eid is a day you dress for. For some, a little perfume too.

Then food, and here's the surprise. Anas reports in al-Bukhari that the Prophet would not go out on the day of the Fitr until he had eaten some dates, in an odd number. For a month, every fast broke at sunset.
This one breaks in daylight, on purpose, before the prayer. Then the prayer itself, together with everyone.
And then the road home, the different one. Why? Scholars have offered reasons: so both roads see the people of the day, so more neighbors get greeted, so more ground bears witness to the prayer.
But Jabir only tells us what he did. The meaning is left open.

how: On the morning of Eid al-Fitr, Muslims often bathe, put on their best clothes, eat a few dates, and go to the Eid prayer together, and some take a different road home afterward, following a report in Sahih al-Bukhari.

practice: In your mind, trace the way you usually come home: the turns, the corners, the same doors you've stopped noticing.

Now find one other way, one street over or the long way round the park, and picture who might be on that road whom you never pass. If you pray, keep the Eid morning walk in mind; if you don't, simply keep the new road ready.

wordCard.voice: Eid al-Fitr. The feast that breaks the fast of Ramadan: a bath, good clothes, dates before the prayer, and a different road back. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name of the feast at the end of Ramadan.

carryVoice: Your line: a new road home. The second road is still there to walk. See you tomorrow.
